children: Sept 15 (Reuters) - Canadian wholesale trade grew by 0.3% in in July from June on higher sales in the building materials and supplies subsector, as well as the food, beverage and tobacco subsector, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday.    Sales were up in three out of seven subsectors, representing 49.7% of wholesale trade, while sales were up in six of the ten provinces. Sales decreased 0.6% in volume terms.

(Percent changes)                               Jul       Jul     Jun (rev)  Jun (prev)                              mo/mo     yr/yr     mo/mo      mo/mo  Wholesale trade             +0.3       +7.9      +2.8       +2.8  Wholesale trade ex-autos     0.0       +9.1      +3.0       +3.2  Wholesale inventories        0.0       +5.5      +1.4       +1.2    Sectors:  Farm products               -1.9       +9.1  Food/beverages/tobacco      +1.7       +3.8          Personal/household          -1.5       +2.1  Motor Vehicles and Parts    +1.7       +2.4  Building materials/supplies +3.5      +14.3  Machinery/equipment         -0.6      +11.1    Misc.                       -2.9      +15.8        NOTE: Figures in the table exclude petroleum and oilseeds sales. All figures are seasonally adjusted. Analysts surveyed by Reuters forecast wholesale trade to be down 0.5% in July from June.
